summary: Round 10 recheck, 26 Sep ~15:20-16:30 UTC. It takes three closed ideas that rounds 2-9 did not re-check. Skipped as already covered: floatout, I-077/78, tempfuse, swapfix, clip-boundary and MIN_TRACK_LEN, axis-flip, head-shift scale, refined-dup collapse, leaf prune, frozen-frame, already-divided, AdaBN, stitch, efpost, linefit, gap LAP/sandwich, zsplit, the headroom family, z-shift, the DivNet veto, the split-flow relink, I-276, the link-stage LB family and I-222. None of the three revives. Finals stay #37 + #38. Nothing was submitted, pushed or committed. (A) I-146, the short-track-filter guard / learned tail rescue ('keep short components with high-p edges'), was closed only by a dependency: 'dominated by the stitch arm, which closed with the edge filter'. NEW FACT: x138 already contains this mechanism as ADAPTIVE_SHORT_TRACK_RESCUE (gates p >= 0.88, mean step <= 3.0 um, 4-5-node components, budget 1.2%/120 nodes). It fires only when the filter removes >= 10% of a clip's nodes, and it fired on 0 of 56 exp60 lab clips and 0 of 4 K2 dummy clips (max removed share 5.3%). MEASURED with the trigger set to 0 (exp60 replay from 'preshort', parity 56/56): pooled +0.00033, nodes +0.22%, edge TP +20 / FP -2, W/L 7/47 clips. Without the one tiny top clip it is +0.00027, and without the top 3 it is +0.00015. The 44b6 SELECTION and CONFIRMATION halves disagree in sign. This is the same lab node-count bias as round 3 (the LB anchor for the same lever is probe 6 at -0.002). It stays closed. The only real change is the reason: the mechanism is already in both finals, dormant on train-like clips. (B) I-097/I-107, the existing fine-tuned primary weights (exp03B, soup) on x138. These weights already exist, so 'no retraining' does not block them, and private scoring is on other embryos. But x138's V1284 head regresses coordinates from the PRIMARY UNet features (the call _v1284_refine(..., unet_out[:, f_idx])). It was trained on pilkwang-primary features, and it raises a hard RuntimeError for any displacement above 2 um. A primary swap would therefore feed the head features it was never trained on. The LB history of primary swaps is +0.004 once on the old pipeline, then -0.003, -0.003 and -0.004. There is no x138 lab bed for a swap, so it cannot meet R8. It stays closed, with a structural blocker added. (C) I-209, matching hidden test clips against public recordings, was closed on 'policy'. The 08:49Z rules check made test-structure use rule-legal, but I-209's reach is zero anyway. The only same-instrument public movie (Ultrack dorado) is the 44b6 TRAIN embryo, and train and test are embryo-disjoint. It stays closed, now on reach.

findings.what: I-146, the short-track-filter guard / learned tail rescue: keep short components whose edges are high-p (adonis122: half of kernel edge FN come from MIN_TRACK_LEN cuts). OLD VERDICT (research/wf_ideas_v2/r1_dedupe.json, ledger I-146): refuted as 'dominated by the stitch fragment-rescue arm, which closed with the edge filter'. It was never measured on its own. WHAT CHANGED: (1) the base is x138, which has no edge filter, so the dominance argument no longer applies; (2) the exp60 x138 lab has a 'preshort' dump, so the filter can be replayed exactly; (3) new fact: x138 ALREADY SHIPS this mechanism. In filter_short_track_components, ADAPTIVE_SHORT_TRACK_RESCUE = 1 and it rescues 4-5-node components with mean edge_prob >= 0.88 and mean step <= 3.0 um, within a budget of min(1.2% of nodes, 120). It is triggered only when the filter removes >= 10% of the clip's nodes. It never fired on the 56 exp60 lab clips (2.19% removed overall, max 5.3%) or on the 4 K2 dummy clips. MEASURED (trigger set to 0, everything else x138's own code; parity 56/56): r88 pooled +0.00033 (SELECTION +0.00028 / CONFIRMATION +0.00038; 44b6 +0.00069, with SEL +0.00125 vs CONF -0.00018; 6bba +0.00030). Nodes +2,479 (+0.22%, 557 components). Edge TP +20 / FP -2 / FN -20, divisions unchanged. W/L 7/47 clips. Three tiny clips carry it (44b6_e35b117d w=278 +0.0103 from 2 TP; 6bba_268e1230 w=619 +4 TP; 6bba_fc5f39dc w=465 +2 TP): without the top clip +0.00027, without the top 3 +0.00015. Arm variants: no budget +0.00033 (nodes +0.27%); p >= 0.95 without budget +0.00011 (W/L 2/33; without the top 3 +0.00004). NEW VERDICT: STAYS CLOSED for the finals and has no post-deadline value as a mechanism. The shape matches the round-3 boundary rescue (+0.00056, W/L 7/47, one tiny clip) and the MIN_TRACK_LEN lab bias, whose LB anchor for the same lever is probe 6 L4 = -0.002. Even taken at face value, +0.0003 lab is about +0.00005 public at the insertion's ~1/6 transfer, far below R4's +0.002, and there is no time before R8 (27 Sep 12:00 UTC). The closure reason changes from 'dominated by stitch' to 'measured ~0 with a node-count bias; the mechanism is already inside x138 and both finals'. Private-scope fact: on hidden clips where the filter removes >= 10% of the nodes (heavy fragmentation), #37 and #38 both rescue up to 120 nodes per clip. The finals share this behaviour, so it is not a hedge difference.

findings.what: I-097 / I-107: the existing fine-tuned primary weights (exp03B = pilkwang primary + 1,200 it on all train videos; soup03B_50) put into the current base. OLD VERDICT: lb-tested. Probe 2 gave +0.004 on the old 0.941 pipeline (0.945), then probes 11 and 15 gave -0.003 each on the sjlee TTA stack and probe 17 (soup) gave -0.004. Every later weight swap was negative ('all 7 LB weight swaps negative', ledger MODEL cluster). The idea was never tried on x138. WHAT COULD REVIVE IT: the weights already exist, so the 'no retraining before 29 Sep' rule does not block them. The private score (~71%) is on other embryos, where a model tuned on both train embryos might transfer differently than on the public embryo. And the 12 h limit leaves ~4 h of headroom. WHAT THE CHECK FOUND: x138's V1284 head is 'frozen-feature coordinate regression at first-seen fused detector centers'. It is patched into the predict script as `arr = _v1284_refine(ds_path, t, arr, unet_out[:, f_idx])`, i.e. it samples the PRIMARY UNet feature map. The head (biohub-v1284-head-s075) was trained on x107's 20-movie capture of pilkwang-primary features, and it raises RuntimeError('invalid V1284 displacement') if any shift exceeds 2 um. The secondary is sha256-pinned. A primary swap therefore (1) feeds the head feature statistics it never saw, so the coordinate head (x138's +0.007 lever) could silently degrade or hard-fail a clip; (2) moves lowrefine (which also head-refines) and the dual-seed retention guard (44b6 33.1% / 6bba 3.9% primary-only frames, round 9); (3) has no x138 lab bed: an exp60-style GPU rerun needs ~5 GPU-h plus a dummy and an OK before R8 (27 Sep 12:00 UTC), and R4 needs +0.002 on public against a 1-for-4 LB record. NEW VERDICT: STAYS CLOSED. The blocker is stronger than before, because it is structural (head-feature coupling) and not only the LB record. Post-deadline, a primary swap on x138 requires retraining the V1284 head on the new primary's features (a retrain item).

findings.what: I-209: match hidden test clips against public recordings (the Ultrack 'dorado' movie) or use public tracks as labels. OLD VERDICT (CONTEXT 23 Sep 23:30 UTC, l.1281-1288; ledger I-209): refuted on POLICY ('against the spirit of the competition and the hosts' statement'). WHAT CHANGED: the 08:49 UTC rules check found that automated use of test-set structure is not prohibited (only hand-labelling or human prediction of test data is, 3.4.b), and that external data is allowed if public. On that basis the user reopened overlap consensus as a candidate (08:58 / 09:10 UTC). So the policy reason behind I-209 no longer holds by itself, and the idea needed a check on reach. CHECK: the only same-instrument, same-scale public recording is the Ultrack dorado movie. It IS the 44b6 TRAIN embryo (tools/register_44b6_dorado.py placed 63 of 71 44b6 clips; 654/777 GT nodes of 44b6_12dfb391 coincide with dorado track points). The Data page says 'Train and test sets are embryo-disjoint'. So dorado cannot contain any hidden-test crop, and no other public recording at our scale is known (research/wf_ideas_v3/h_external-data-training.json). NEW VERDICT: STAYS CLOSED, now on zero reach and not on policy. Any remaining version (searching other Zebrahub movies for the hidden embryos) is TB-scale, needs new code and an uploaded dataset, cannot meet R8, and would carry the fairness question of rules 3.14.a / 3.8.d. This correction matters mostly for the lessons and for the curator: the 08:49 rules check does not reopen I-209.
